Psychiatry has it's place, but has been given far too much clout.

The issue is that the relative foundation for psychiatry is weaker than other medical fields that it can be compared to mostly due to the complexity of the brain and until recently the lack of tools necessary to study the biology of the situation on any scale remotely close to what we have been able to do with the rest of the body for a long time.

There is good reason for the transition toward a more biological basis of diagnosis [OC] that has been beginning recently and has support from the National Institute of Mental Health.

That said, despite its flaws Psychiatry as it functions today is the best we've got and, the few instances of its failings notwithstanding, is much better than not doing anything.

The real issue is that it is compared to more modern medicine but in reality it should be compared more to early to mid 20th century medicine because until recently the tools we had for studying the brain and its relation to mental health issues were comparable to the tech used then for things like cardiovascular health then. But given the choice between no healthcare and 1950's healthcare I would choose 1950's healthcare every time.

Certainly, I do love some of the insights it brings to light. It's also been proven to be quite an effective weapon, not that speaks to the ill of it. However, we shouldn't forget that it is a relatively fledgling science and we still fail to understand the vast majority of the mind. In my opinion, it too often tries to 'treat' those that just vary from the norm.
